content.title: USPS postal inspector jobs open as FERS contributions paused
content.text: USPS hiring postal inspectors as it suspends FERS contributions to conserve cash.jetcityimage/Getty ImagesThe U.S. Postal Service is hiring inspectors nationwide, even as it pauses certain retirement contributions amid what it has described as an ongoing severe financial crisis.On April 9, USPS announced a cash conservation plan that includes temporarily suspending its employer contributions to the Federal Employees Retirement System, a key component of federal retirement benefits.Article continues below this adGet Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.Get Digital Access and Stay Informed With Trusted Local News.ONLY 25¢The agency typically contributes about $200 million every two weeks to the Office of Personnel Management for FERS annuities. Officials say the suspension, which took effect April 10, is expected to free up nearly $2.5 billion during the current fiscal year.“There will not be any immediate detrimental impact to current or future retirees if FERS cost payments are temporarily withheld,” said Postal Service Chief Financial Officer Luke Grossmann. “The risk to the Postal Service and the public from insufficient liquidity for operations outweighs any longer-term risk to the pension funds. We will continue to transmit employees’ FERS contributions, as well as employer and employee contributions to the Thrift Savings Plan, and our pension systems remain better funded than those of many other agencies.”What is a U.S. Postal Inspector?Postal inspectors are federal law enforcement officers responsible for protecting the integrity of the U.S. mail and ensuring the safety of Postal Service employees and customers.Article continues below this adAccording to the agency, postal inspectors enforce more than 200 laws aimed at stopping drug trafficking, money laundering, threats, cybercrime, and identity and financial fraud. They also work to prevent dangerous or hazardous materials from being sent through the mail.Who can apply?Applicants must:Article continues below this ad Be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident. Meet the physical requirements. Possess a four-year degree from an accredited academic institution (exceptions apply for veterans with equivalent experience). Be willing to travel. Be between the ages of 21 and 37. Have no felony or domestic violence convictions. How to applyTo apply, visit the U.S. Postal Inspection Service hiring portal at www.uspis.gov/careers.Application deadlineApplications are open until Thursday, April 23, 2026.Article continues below this adFor more information, visit www.uspis.gov.Don't miss news and stories you need to read.April 16, 2026Crystal Huggins is a 2023 graduate of Delta College with an associate’s degree in electronic media broadcasting. During her time at Delta, she gained hands-on experience in media production and was recognized for her academic achievements, earning multiple honors. She has worked as a news producer and anchor for NEWSnet, where she delivered daily broadcasts for audiences in Hawaii, Northern Michigan, and Los Angeles. She also has experience in radio broadcasting, having served as a morning show producer and on-air personality for MacDonald Broadcasting. A mid-Michigan resident, Crystal is passionate about storytelling, multimedia content creation, and engaging audiences through digital and social media platforms.
